target: Pinned Primer React Dialog root semantic role, accessible ID relationships and conditional subtitle
observed_behavior: In this pinned Dialog implementation, _Dialog defaults its role prop to 'dialog', while its role type allows 'dialog' or 'alertdialog'. The generated label and description IDs are passed to a root div rendered in a Portal with role={role}, aria-labelledby, aria-describedby and aria-modal (present as a boolean attribute). DefaultHeader gives Dialog.Title the label ID and renders Dialog.Subtitle with the description ID only when subtitle is truthy. When subtitle is absent, the root still sets aria-describedby to the generated description ID, without DefaultHeader rendering a matching subtitle element. A supplied header renderer or header slot can also replace the default elements. This records JSX structure and conditional branches, not demonstrated accessible-name or screen-reader behavior.

limitations: The unconditional aria-describedby root attribute versus conditional DefaultHeader subtitle means a description target cannot be presumed present when subtitle is falsey; do not silently claim robust description association for every prop combination.
Custom renderHeader/header slots can change the title/description target markup; their exact output is not established by this file alone.
Role and ARIA JSX source code do not establish browser accessibility-tree exposure, accessible-name computation, runtime focus behavior or WCAG conformance.
